responsibility: Is the sole call path from CIS to any execution backend and refuses to dispatch without a verified ALLOW.
mutation_interface: none — it appends runs, evidence and trajectory events only through the modules that own them
failure_boundary: fail_closed — unknown authorization, non-recomputing binding, non-ALLOW verdict, stale objective, moved baseline, undeclared operation, unavailable backend, missing or malformed mandatory policy envelope, mismatched task-contract or selector binding, widened policy scope, unsupported policy obligations, incomplete authorization preflight, missing performed checks, or policy evidence not returned exactly as label=verified all refuse
recovery_behavior: Every refusal is appended as a trajectory event and an atomic attempt claim remains after adapter entry, so an interrupted attempt leaves evidence rather than silence and recovery requires a new authorization
replacement_contract: A replacement must build the request from recorded authorization rather than caller input, require and independently recompute a current policy envelope for adapters that declare it mandatory, refuse obligations outside the adapter's declared closed support, merge restrictions into the token-covered request, require exact label=verified result evidence, atomically claim the authorization before adapter entry, and issue a single-use capability only after that claim; the operation is never a dispatch argument
evidence_produced: execution_dispatched, execution_completed and execution_refused trajectory events
atomic execution_attempt_claims row before adapter entry
backend_runs row with opaque adapter id and request hash after a result
